name: DRPC
workload: In-process microbenchmark of unary, input-stream, output-stream, and bidirectional-stream RPC calls at three payload sizes (small/medium/large), no real network transport involved
claimed_speedup: Unary latency -68% to -72% (e.g. small: 29.7us->8.3us, large: 1.70ms->0.54ms); throughput +214% to +243% (e.g. large unitary: 618MB/s->1939MB/s)
stars_or_usage: 1.6k stars; author states it is used in production across tens of thousands of Storj servers
tradeoffs: Smaller feature surface than gRPC (fewer official language implementations, some marked Incomplete); microbenchmark is in-process only, so it excludes the network/transport cost that dominates real RPC latency
caveats: The README explicitly states the benchmark was not run in a controlled environment (CPU scaling not disabled, not noiseless) and that the comparison inherently favors DRPC because its author is more familiar with its internals -- capped at tier C for these self-admitted methodology gaps
found_via: HN Algolia query 'faster than gRPC' surfaced a BRPC thread mentioning gRPC alternatives; followed up by opening storj/drpc directly and reading its README Benchmarks section

name: cmd-stream-go (MUS codec over TCP)
workload: 1/2/4/8/16 concurrent Go clients sending echo requests over TCP, payload sizes 17-1024 bytes, fixed 30ms server-side delay per request, QPS measured with go test -bench
claimed_speedup: 288,727 QPS (cmd-stream/MUS/TCP) vs 63,285 QPS (gRPC/HTTP2/protobuf) at 16 clients, roughly 4.6x higher (derived from page data)
compiler_and_flags: Go 1.24.1, `GEN_SIZE=400000 go test -bench BenchmarkQPS -count=10 -timeout=30m` (default build flags)
hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 5850U with Radeon Graphics, Debian 6.1.148-1 x86_64
stars_or_usage: cmd-stream-go: 94 stars; benchmark suite (ymz-ncnk/go-client-server-benchmarks) is an independent third-party repo, 17 stars
tradeoffs: MUS is a custom binary encoding requiring its own codegen/marshaling code, with a smaller ecosystem than Protobuf; benchmark run on a single laptop (with charger and fan at full speed per its own notes), not an isolated server
caveats: cmd-stream/cmd-stream-go is already on KNOWN_LIST; reported here only because this is new Tier A third-party evidence for it (independent benchmark repo with public code, stated compiler/Go version, and stated CPU/OS), per the orchestrator's is_evidence_for_known exception
found_via: HN Algolia query 'faster than gRPC' surfaced 'Cmd-stream/MUS is about 3 times faster than gRPC/Protobuf' pointing to https://github.com/ymz-ncnk/go-client-server-benchmarks; opened that repo's README and results/qps/qps.csv

name: Lightstream
workload: Streaming RAM-resident Apache Arrow tables (numeric, mixed, string-heavy, wide schemas; 1M rows/batch from a 300GB pool) between two AWS instances over a 50 Gbit/s network, across multiple levels of connection parallelism
claimed_speedup: Lightstream leads Arrow Flight in every measured workload-shape/parallelism combination in the published results table; per-cell warm-median throughput ratios given, not a single aggregate number (derived from page data)
hardware: 2x AWS i3en.12xlarge instances in one placement group, 50 Gbit/s network
tradeoffs: Purpose-built for bulk columnar Arrow-table transport, not a general RPC replacement; Lightstream reconstructs one globally-ordered stream across parallel connections, a cost the README says it 'wears' in its own reported numbers, while Arrow Flight orders only per-endpoint
caveats: Baseline is Arrow Flight (built on gRPC/HTTP2), not bare gRPC, so this is a proxy comparison; compiler/toolchain flags are stated for a separate single-machine microbenchmark in the same README but not restated for this specific cross-host AWS benchmark; project is only days old with no independent reproduction yet
found_via: gh search repos 'websocket "faster than"' surfaced SpaceCell/lightstream ('Measured faster than Arrow Flight on all open benchmarks'); opened repo README and rust/README.md benchmark section

name: fRPC (frpc-go)
workload: Echo RPC service benchmark at 32-byte, 512-byte, and 128KB message sizes with up to 8192 concurrent clients on a local network, plus a variant adding 50-microsecond simulated blocking server work
claimed_speedup: ~3-4x higher throughput than gRPC across tested message sizes; server handling >2,000,000 RPCs/sec vs gRPC's <500,000 RPCs/sec at 8192 clients (derived from page data)
hardware: 2x AMD EPYC 7643 48-core CPUs, 256GB DDR4 memory, local network
tradeoffs: fRPC was still Alpha per its own README (missing OneOf message types); relies on the loopholelabs/frisbee-go messaging layer; smaller ecosystem/tooling maturity than gRPC
caveats: Benchmark is hosted on the project's own docs site (first-party); hardware is stated but compiler version, language runtime, and build flags are not; the linked reproducible-benchmark repo (loopholelabs/frpc-go-benchmarks) is archived
found_via: HN Algolia query 'faster than gRPC' surfaced 'Show HN: FRPC - A Faster, More Flexible RPC Framework'; opened https://frpc.io/performance/grpc-benchmarks for the numbers
